deck_title: Quilez ellipsoid SDF gradient Lipschitz normalization vs naive non-uniform scale overstep rig

cards.subtitle: Deterministic Inigo Quilez (2019 "Ellipsoids SDF") & John C. Hart (SIGGRAPH 1989 "Sphere Tracing") gradient-normalized ellipsoid distance bound (k0 = ||p/r||, k1 = ||p/r^2||, d_IQ(p) = k0*(k0 - 1)/k1, locking Lipschitz step-to-true-distance ratio L_IQ = 1.0000x) versus naive non-uniformly scaled unit-sphere SDF (d_naive(p) = ||p/r|| - 1, inflating step ratio by kappa = 1/r_min up to 5.0000x) and 64-iteration Newton-Lagrange closest-point root finding across 17 compression ratios (kappa in [1.0000, 5.0000]).

cards.headline: Exact controls are useful; realism remains a separate job.
good_fit: Raymarching (Sphere Tracing) of ellipsoids, capsules, petals, and non-uniformly scaled SDF primitives without overstep tunneling (Quilez 2019 / Hart 1989)
SDF soft shadows, ambient occlusion, and collision thickness probes requiring isotropic Euclidean distance bounds around thin axes
Closed-form dual-norm ratio k0*(k0-1)/k1 avoiding 6th-degree polynomial root finding
2-norm algebraic evaluation replacing 64-iteration Newton-Lagrange closest-point solvers
not_for: Uniformly scaled spheres (r_x = r_y = r_z = R) where length(p) - R is already an exact unit-gradient SDF
